body.en: India was among the first countries in the world to start action plans for reproductive health at the national level: family planning began in 1951. Improved and wider *programmes* are now called Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes. They create awareness through audio-visual and print media, introduce sex education in schools, and educate couples about birth control, care of pregnant mothers, post-natal care, breastfeeding and equal opportunities for boys and girls.

title.en: Birth rate, death rate and growth
title.kn: ಜನನ ದರ, ಮರಣ ದರ ಮತ್ತು ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ

narration.en: India's population was about 36 crore in 1947. Better health care cut the death rate, but the birth rate stayed high, so the population grew fast. Set the birth and death rates (per 1,000 people per year) and see the growth rate, the doubling time (about 70 ÷ growth %) and the population after 50 years. India's family planning programmes aim to bring the birth rate down.
narration.kn: 1947 ರಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾರತದ ಜನಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಸುಮಾರು 36 ಕೋಟಿ. ಉತ್ತಮ ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ಸೇವೆ ಮರಣ ದರ ಇಳಿಸಿತು, ಆದರೆ ಜನನ ದರ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗಿಯೇ ಉಳಿದು ಜನಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಬೆಳೆಯಿತು. ಜನನ ಮತ್ತು ಮರಣ ದರ (ವರ್ಷಕ್ಕೆ 1,000 ಜನರಿಗೆ) ಹೊಂದಿಸಿ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆಯ ದರ, ದ್ವಿಗುಣ ಕಾಲ (≈ 70 ÷ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ %) ಮತ್ತು 50 ವರ್ಷದ ನಂತರದ ಜನಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ನೋಡಿ.

body.en: *Amniocentesis* is a foetal sex-determination test based on the chromosomal pattern in the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing embryo. It is meant to detect genetic disorders, but it was misused to find the sex of the foetus and abort female foetuses. India has a statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination, to curb female foeticide. Better awareness has reduced maternal and infant mortality and increased medically assisted deliveries.
body.kn: ಆಮ್ನಿಯೋಸೆಂಟೆಸಿಸ್ ಆಮ್ನಿಯೋಟಿಕ್ ದ್ರವದ ವರ್ಣತಂತು ಮಾದರಿಯಿಂದ ಭ್ರೂಣದ ಆನುವಂಶಿಕ ದೋಷ ಪತ್ತೆ ಮಾಡುವ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ. ಲಿಂಗ ನಿರ್ಧಾರಕ್ಕೆ ಇದರ ಬಳಕೆಗೆ ಕಾನೂನು ನಿಷೇಧವಿದೆ.

tagline.en: What reproductive health means, India's RCH programmes, and the growth of population.

say.en: India launched family planning in 1951. Improved programmes covering wider reproduction-related areas are today called Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes.

The main causes of rapid growth were a fast decline in the death rate, maternal mortality rate (MMR) and infant mortality rate (IMR), along with more people of reproductive age. Census 2011 put India's growth rate at less than 2%, i.e. about 20 per 1000 per year.
